headline: Base rate hike and customer growth drive higher earnings
summary_short: IDACORP's Q2 2026 revenue rose 4.2% y/y (+16.5% q/q, seasonal) to $469.8M and diluted EPS was $1.79 (+1.7% y/y, +47.9% q/q), as new Idaho base rates and customer growth lifted operating income, partly offset by a smaller prior-year ADITC tax credit.
summary_long: Revenue rose 4.2% y/y (+16.5% q/q) to $469.8M as the January 2026 Idaho base-rate increase added $27.5M to operating income and customer growth (+2.3% over the trailing twelve months) added $4.5M, with large-contract customers adding $6.5M. These gains were partly offset by $11.7M higher Other O&M (deferred Jim Bridger coal-to-gas conversion and wildfire-mitigation amortization, both rate-recovered) and $5.2M higher depreciation. Net income rose 7.1% y/y to $102.6M ($1.79 diluted EPS, +1.7% y/y); the smaller y/y EPS gain reflects the absence of $17.2M of additional ADITC amortization booked in Q2 2025. IDACORP guides 2026 capex to $1.3-1.5B, 2027 to $1.4-1.6B, and 2028-2030 to $3.6-4.1B, funded via a $350M February first-mortgage-bond issuance and multiple 2026 ATM equity settlements.

drivers.explanation: Idaho base rates effective January 1, 2026 added $27.5M to operating income; customer growth (+2.3% y/y) added $4.5M; large-contract customers added $6.5M on higher usage and one new contract effective June 1, 2026.

Rate and customer-growth gains were partly offset by $11.7M higher Other O&M (deferred Jim Bridger coal-to-gas conversion costs and wildfire-mitigation amortization, both rate-recovered) and $5.2M higher depreciation from increased plant-in-service.
Y/y net income growth was tempered by the absence of $17.2M of additional ADITC amortization booked in Q2 2025 under Idaho's regulatory settlement, which increased income tax expense this quarter.
Diluted EPS grew slower than net income y/y (+1.7% vs +7.1%) because weighted-average diluted shares rose to 57.2M from 54.4M on 2026 ATM and forward-sale-agreement equity issuances.

Company guides a multi-year capital program: 2026 capex $1.3-1.5B, 2027 $1.4-1.6B, 2028-2030 $3.6-4.1B, for transmission (B2H, SWIP-N, GWW) and new gas/solar/storage generation, funded via first-mortgage bonds and ATM/forward equity issuances.
